Subject: Pilot MAP - observability retention and evaluation cadence

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Based on our conversation, I drafted a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to align timelines and the evaluation milestones for the BrightLayer pilot. Key questions before I send a formal MAP:

- Confirmation on pilot scope: 3 evaluation workloads (search summarization, fine-grained reranking, embeddings for similarity).
- Target pilot duration: 6 weeks, with an interim review at week 3.
- Observability requirements: you mentioned extended retention during evaluation — is 90 days acceptable, or do you need 180?

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Grace (solutions) to put together the milestone-based pricing options that map to commits/ramp (pilot -> POC -> initial commit). We can also include premium support credits and short-term observability retention as a bundled add-on during the evaluation.

Proposed next step: quick 30-min sync Wednesday to finalize scope.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks

Dylan —

Thanks — Wednesday works. Quick answers inline:
- Pilot scope: yes, that covers the core use cases.
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks with week-3 check is perfect.
- Observability: for initial analysis we need 180 days of retention for traces/metrics for one of the evaluation workloads (the reranking service). For the others 90 days is fine.

Also, procurement will want to understand: what pricing commitments would be required to secure extended retention and premium support credits? If you can show a MAP that ties pricing/discounts to commits (e.g., 3-month committed baseline after successful pilot -> X% discount; 12-month commit -> deeper discount + observability included), that’ll help get internal buy-in.

Perfect — thanks for the clarity, Emily. Looping in Grace (solutions engineering) and Vivek (product sales engineering) to draft a MAP that ties milestones to commercial terms.

High-level we can propose:
- Pilot (6 weeks): no commit, usage-based billing, temporary add-ons for extended observability for the reranking workload (180 days) as a trial courtesy.
- Post-pilot (initial commit): 3-month committed capacity (discounted) if success criteria met at week 6 (latency and quality gates).
- Ramp/scale: 12-month commitment option for sustained production deployment with deeper discounts + bundled observability retention (90 days by default, 180 days for critical workloads) and a set amount of premium support credits.

We’ll produce a versioned MAP doc with milestone-linked pricing bands and suggested acceptance criteria for the pilot (latency, token cost per request, approximation of per-minute throughput). Grace — can you take point on the MAP spreadsheet and include a sample SOW that reflects the add-on packages (observability retention, premium support credits, add-on credits for embeddings)?

I’ll aim to get a draft over by Friday EOD.

Thanks,
Dylan

Subject: MAP + SOW draft for BrightLayer pilot (v1)

Hi Emily —

Attaching a first pass MAP and SOW that maps milestones to commercial outcomes. Highlights:

1) Pilot (Weeks 0–6) — Evaluation
   - Scope: 3 workloads, up to 2M tokens/day aggregate.
   - Observability: 180-day retention for reranking traces (one dataset), 90 days for others (courtesy trial).
   - Cost: usage-based, covered by BrightLayer evaluation credits up to $8k.
   - Success criteria: 95th pctl latency within 150ms (reranking), generation quality passing internal evals.

2) Initial Commit (post-pilot, Months 0–3) — Small commitment
   - Commit: monthly reserved throughput equivalent to 3M tokens/month.
   - Pricing: 15% discount off hosted list pricing for the committed baseline.
   - Add-ons on success: one-time allocation of 40 premium support credits (to be used for L3 debugging/priority triage).

3) Production Ramp (Months 4–15) — 12-month option
   - Commit: annual commit (12 months) with scaling clauses.
   - Pricing: 30% discount on baseline + included observability retention bundle (90 days standard, half of workloads eligible for 180 days) + 200 premium support credits spread across the term.
   - Credits: additional add-on credits purchasable at pre-negotiated rate.

Attachments included: MAP_BrightLayer_v1.xlsx (milestone timeline + acceptance), SOW_BrightLayer_v1.pdf (contract language stub).

Open items we flagged in the doc:
- Exact metrics for "quality passing internal evals" (Grace to propose pass/fail thresholds).
- Whether procurement needs a PO or DocuSign agreement up front for initial commit.
- Billing cadence (monthly invoice vs net-30).

Emily — if the commercial bands look reasonable I can iterate to align language with your procurement team.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_BrightLayer_v1.xlsx; SOW_BrightLayer_v1.pdf

Subject: Re: MAP + SOW draft for BrightLayer pilot (v1)

Thanks Grace — the MAP is a helpful starting point. A few procurement asks before we can move to sign:

1) Can the 180-day retention for reranking be extended to 240 days for the pilot artifact store? We need slightly longer for regulatory sampling during evaluation.
2) Procurement prefers a short-term credit for premium support specifically reserved for onboarding (rather than a general pool). Can you carve out 60 support credits for onboarding only?
3) We’d like the option to convert evaluation usage credits into a portion of the initial commit (applied as pre-paid credit) if we sign within 30 days of pilot completion.

If you can accept those three items, procurement is happy to proceed with a DocuSign SOW and a standard PO for the initial 3-month commit. Looping procurement on this thread for transparency.

—Emily
